pr_title: Print warning when optimizations are disabled
pr_body:
# Objective
Fixes #1827

## Solution

- Check optimization level of bevy_ecs
- Print warning on startup
- ~Should the warning mention that you can enable optimizations for dependencies even in debug mode?~
pr_comments:
> Should the warning mention that you can enable optimizations for dependencies even in debug mode?

This should be the default and `--release` should not be mentioned. It's nice for quickly seeing if perf is the issue, but it really shouldn't be used unless you are actually building for release. I would suggest simply linking the page on the website that explains this.

In general, I'm not sure this is required though, bevy still works fine without optimization for quickly testing stuff and adding a warning for this feels a bit too much.

> This should be the default and --release should not be mentioned. It's nice for quickly seeing if perf is the issue, but it really shouldn't be used unless you are actually building for release. I would suggest simply linking the page on the website that explains this.

Yeah, that sounds better.

> In general, I'm not sure this is required though, bevy still works fine without optimization for quickly testing stuff and adding a warning for this feels a bit too much.

Opinions were pretty positive on the issue. I'm not to fuzzed either way if we want to close it.
Is the build script really necessary? It seems it's putting the value from env var `OPT_LEVEL` in env var `OPT_LEVEL`?

> Is the build script really necessary? It seems it's putting the value from env var `OPT_LEVEL` in env var `OPT_LEVEL`?

Unfortunately, `OPT_LEVEL` is only available in the build script.
I still dislike build scripts, but it does what it's supposed to 👍
Marked as controversial and ready for final review. This is well made and does what it's supposed to, but I'm not sure that any of us are convinced it's worth the tech debt :)
I'm going to close this out. I like this conceptually, but I don't think its worth adding build.rs into the mix.

Should #1827 be closed as well? Altough I guess one could alternatively try to parse `Cargo.toml` and look for the relevant configuration and then use `cfg(debug_assertions)`, though that would be more complicated and perhaps more error-prone.

issue_context.title: Warn on startup when Bevy itself is built without optimizations
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

Without optimizations Bevy is slow. Not everyone realizes that they can use `--release` to drastically improve performance. This is a frequent topic on the Discord.

## What solution would you like?

See title. This can be implemented by adding a build script to a crate like `bevy_app` that reads the `OPT_LEVEL` env var. And when the value is 0 causes a startup system to be enabled that prints a warning suggesting to pass `--release`.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

Somehow teach Cargo to always optimize Bevy and it's dependencies.

## Additional context

https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/742884593551802431/828710614721363969
comments:
I think logging a message under [`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#debug-assertions) rather than a build script would be nicer.

There's also the [`env`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.env.html) macro to read env at compile time to do this, but without conditional compilation.
You can enable debug assertions and optimizations at the same time. Using the `env!` macro doesn't work here as `OPT_LEVEL` is only set for build scripts. Not when building with rustc.
I would like to avoid a build script as they often make compilation longer / harder to cache...

Using `println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");` should ensure that the build script doesn't run on any changes to the crate source by switching from the legacy "any source change => re-run" to "specified source change => re-run". The build script is very simple so it doesn't require any dependencies. This allows it to run at the start of the compilation at the same time as other crates without dependencies.
Closing per #7698. The complexity here is too high for the benefits.

review_comments: this would mean the script wouldn't rerun if the env var `OPT_LEVEL` changed
From my testing, cargo reruns the build script when the profile is configured differently.
I don't understand how this works: why does println do anything here?

Build scripts [communicate with Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#outputs-of-the-build-script) via stdout. This line tells cargo not to rerun the build script when files are changed (unless some settings or the script itself has changed).
